about-me-headline.purpose: Big Shoulders Display 900, uppercase: Section titles in the Display colour.

about-me-title.purpose: Big Shoulders Display 800, uppercase: item titles and the Footer's title.

about-me-billing.purpose: Archivo 800, uppercase: the items of a lineup, in the band's ink. --text-billing is named in both sets; the title size on the Portfolio.

about-me-lede.purpose: One line under the Page title, 52ch measure.

about-me-body.purpose: Stories and notes in the band's ink, 68ch measure.

about-me-small.purpose: 400: notes and a field's hint; controls and error messages take it at the control weight (700).

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Controls, row links, switch options. 0ms under reduced motion.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Panel hover edge and wash. 0ms under reduced motion.

motion.name: duration-theme
motion.purpose: Theme crossfade of every token at once, except the theme switch, which only slides its pressed fill. 0ms under reduced motion.

motion.name: duration-spin
motion.purpose: One turn of the loading ring, on ease-linear. 0ms under reduced motion, where the ring fades instead.

motion.name: duration-pulse
motion.purpose: One fade of the loading ring under reduced motion, which replaces its turn. Kept under reduced motion: the one animation left there, with no movement.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only transition easing: exponential ease-out, no bounce.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: The loading ring's fade under reduced motion, which runs both ways.

motion.name: ease-linear
motion.purpose: The loading ring's turn. Under reduced motion its fade loops on ease-in-out instead.

motion.name: press-offset
motion.purpose: How far a pressed control sinks: both Buttons and the action Link, never the plain Link. 0px under reduced motion.

motion.name: nudge
motion.purpose: How far a link's arrow moves on hover, focus and press. About me sets 3px. 0px under reduced motion.

motion.name: pulse-opacity
motion.purpose: The loading ring's faintest point as it fades under reduced motion: 3:1 or more on every theme and band (the secondary on About me's sunset needs 0.68).

states.name: disabled

components.name: Role Entry
components.description: One role on Experience, and the Portfolio's only (About me never shows one). On narrow screens the head (the title, a heading at the level the page needs, and the company), the meta (period, location, work model) and the body (summary, achievements, Chips) stack in that order, 0.75rem apart, so the meta never sits above the title as an eyebrow. From 44rem the meta takes a side column (--role-entry-side-width, 12rem) down both rows, beside the head and then the body, 0.75rem by 2rem apart. The meta is Small in Muted Ink, one item per line, 0.5rem apart; only the period takes the Label role (monospace, uppercase, tabular numerals), while location and work model stay in the sans, as the Facts panel sets them. The title is in the Title role, the company 0.25rem under it in Body at the control weight, the summary and achievements in Body in Secondary Ink at the measure (a disc list with Muted Ink markers), then the technologies as Chips. Every part is required, as the Vision lists them for every role; the layout still holds when the location, work model, achievements or technologies are missing, so a gap never breaks it. Consecutive .role-entry siblings share a Hairline with 2rem above and below it, so a page that wraps entries in list items keeps them siblings or moves the rule to the item. Every word is Content except the dates' month names and "present", which follow the chosen language. The Owner chose a side column over a stacked entry and a hairline panel per role, and only the period in monospace over an all-monospace column. Static: no states. Needs the Chip. An item has a head (the name in the Title role, then the source in Body at the control weight, 0.25rem apart), a meta (the date in the Label role, then a place or an optional credential ID, both Small Muted Ink in the sans, 0.5rem apart) and an optional body (a note in Body in Secondary Ink, or a credential Link). On narrow screens head, meta and body stack 0.5rem apart, so a date never sits above the name; from 44rem the meta takes the side column the Role entry uses (--role-entry-side-width, 12rem, 0.25rem top padding) beside the head and body, 2rem apart. Consecutive items share a Hairline with 1.5rem above and below it, tighter than a Role entry's 2rem. Fields (the Owner's): Education shows name, institution, period, location and an optional note; a Certification shows name, issuer, issue date, an optional credential ID and an optional credential link. The Owner chose items like a Role entry over compact rows and hairline cards, a small heading, and the ID in the sans. Every word is Content except month names and "present". Static: the Link keeps its states. Needs the Link. Built in prototype/components/qualification-list/.

components.name: Lineup
components.description: About me's billing rows, and About me's only (the Portfolio never shows one), shown on the lime band: the wrapper sets every token the sample reads to the lime band's resolved values, so it renders standalone, and the lineup takes everything from tokens. Two 3px rules in Key close the list; each row stacks a category (display face, Category role, uppercase, hyphenating when longer than its column, or breaking mid-word where the browser has no hyphenation dictionary) over its items (Billing type in the band's ink), 0.5rem apart, in one column a long word breaks inside rather than widens, and from 36rem sets them in a --lineup-category-width (14rem) column and the rest on a shared baseline. A category's items, a list of one or more, run in a row that wraps, 0.5rem down; each item leads with a drawn square (--lineup-separator-size, 0.25em) in the row's key colour, centred on the capitals, 0.75rem from the item before it and 0.75rem from its own, and the list starts that far before its column and clips the square off whichever item starts a line, so a square only sits between two items; an item that wraps continues under its first letter, and a screen reader reads only the items. Rows sit 1.5rem apart, wider than a category's wrapped items, so each category reads as one group. Odd rows take Key and even rows Key Alt through --row-key. An item is a link only when the Owner gives it an address and then rests on a thin underline (--lineup-rest-line-width, 1px) in its row's key colour, thickening to the line width (3px) on hover, focus and press (a pressed item looks like a hovered one); focus adds the 3px ring. A plain item has no underline and no hover. No disabled. Built in prototype/components/lineup/.

narrative.overview:
The Portfolio's Visual language is a dark, confident engineering page where bold, tightly tracked type and hairline panels carry the authority and the facts lead. The Owner stays in the background: a small, plain photo beside the name, never a portrait as the centrepiece.

The Portfolio's Visual language is monochrome bone and ink. Dark is the default, always: a near-black ground carries warm bone ink. The complete light theme puts the same ink on bone paper and appears only when the visitor picks it in the dark and light switch, never from the system preference. Every colour token resolves both themes through `light-dark()`, so the active colour scheme picks one. Secondary text, metadata, hairlines and tints are the ink itself at fixed alpha steps; there is no hued accent anywhere. The primary action is the ink, filled; focus is an ink ring. The only hue in the system is error.

About me has its own, entirely distinct Visual language. It restyles the shared navigation, language toggle and Footer through tokens alone; their place and behavior never change.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default, always; light a complete equal the visitor switches to; both WCAG 2.2 AA.
Monochrome: bone ink on near-black, ink on bone paper, secondary ink and hairlines by alpha steps of the ink.

No hued accent: the primary action is filled ink, every other button is outlined in a hairline, row links are unboxed text (the Side navigation's Toggle-like entries and the Content item row, a whole row that leads into its editor, are rows this doesn't cover), focus is an ink ring.
Bold display grotesk with tight tracking; monospace only for labels, tags, chips and numerals.
Hairline-bordered panel grids whose cells share borders, instead of cards and shadows.
Facts over the person: the role and seniority lead Home as its largest type, beside a hairline facts panel; the photo stays small.

rules.name: The Ink Is The Action Rule
rules.body: There is no accent colour. The primary action is the ink filled, with the ground as its text: one per view. Secondary buttons are outlined in Hairline Control; row links stay unboxed (the Side navigation's Toggle-like entries and the Content item row, a whole row that leads into its editor, are rows this rule doesn't cover). Focus is an ink ring. If a view needs colour to show what to do next, the hierarchy is wrong, not the palette.

rules.name: The Alpha Steps Rule
rules.body: Secondary, muted, hairline and tint colours are always the ink mixed toward transparent at their fixed steps (84, 64, 26, 22, 10, 7, 4), and the Wash is the ink at 2% mixed into the ground; never new greys. The exceptions are few and named: input borders, set per theme to hold 3:1 (52% ink on paper, 44% bone on night); the raised surfaces (Night Raised, Paper Raised); and the float shadow, whose ring and shadow are the ink at 6% and 22% on paper and bone at 30% over black at 60% on night, because no ink is darker than the night ground.

rules.name: The Only Hue Is Error Rule
rules.body: Error is the sole hued colour, and it appears only where something went wrong.

rules.name: The Two Equal Themes Rule
rules.body: Every colour token exists in both themes and passes AA in both; dark is designed first, never light inverted.

rules.name: The Mono Labels Rule
rules.body: Monospace sets labels, tags, chips and numerals, never sentences or headings, and never as an eyebrow above a heading: the heading carries its own weight.

rules.name: The Hairline Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: Reach for a hairline or a tint step first; a shadow is the last resort and only for something floating above the page.

dos: Do design the dark theme first and keep the light theme a complete equal, both at WCAG 2.2 AA.
Do open every Page in dark; show light only after the visitor picks it in the switch.
Do make the one primary action per view filled ink, and outline every other button in a hairline.
Do derive every secondary, muted, hairline and tint colour from the ink at its fixed alpha step.

Do lead Home with the facts: the role and seniority as the Masthead's largest type, and location, work model and technologies in the hairline facts panel beside it; keep the Owner's photo small and plain beside the name.
Do take every visual value from tokens, so About me can restyle the shared navigation, language toggle and Footer through tokens alone.
Do give every component all its states (default, hover, focus, active, disabled, and loading, error or success where they apply) before it counts as done.
Do keep the Top bar's Pages and Toggles visible at every width: wrap the Toggles under the Pages rather than hide them in a menu.
Do move the theme switch's pressed fill to the option pressed next by sliding one indicator, not by fading between options; the language toggle loads its Page with the fill already in place.

Do keep motion to short expo ease-out transitions (150ms for controls, 200ms for panels, 240ms for the theme crossfade), no bounce, and 0ms under reduced motion. The one loop is the loading ring, on the linear ease (`--ease-linear`); under reduced motion nothing moves, and the ring alone fades instead of turning.
donts: Don't introduce a hued accent, a gradient or a multi-colour palette; the Owner turned down every one offered.
Don't use error red for anything but errors.
Don't follow the system colour scheme preference; the Owner chose dark always by default.
Don't build a template portfolio: no avatar hero, no skill pills, no grid of identical project cards.
Don't set a monospace eyebrow above a heading, or monospace prose.
Don't put a name or logo in the Top bar; the Owner chose a bar of Pages and Toggles only.
Don't let anything come before the repository link in the Footer but its title.
Don't set a Portfolio list as a Lineup; it is About me's only.
Don't make the Owner's photo a centrepiece: no large portrait, no colour effects, no full-bleed photo.
Don't put a shadow on anything that doesn't float above the page.
Don't give a field a placeholder, on either Visual language; the hint carries any example.
Don't let expression cost the 30-second read: role, seniority, technologies, location, CV and contact stay findable at a glance.

aboutMe.overview:
About me's Visual language sets the Owner's interests, recommendations and studies like a gig poster: flat colour bands, one per Section, a condensed uppercase display that runs the band's width, and lists set as a poster's billing. It is loud and warm where the Portfolio is quiet, and it never looks like a social profile, a gamer costume, the Portfolio recoloured, or anything corporate or cold.

It loads over the Portfolio's tokens and redefines the same names, so the shared components take its look through tokens alone. Spacing and motion stay the Portfolio's, except a longer link nudge (3px), a wider chip gap (0.5rem) and a Toggle with no inset to clear its 3px rules, and no gap above a Section heading, which has no rule. It has one theme and no photo. Each band sets every colour token itself, so a component inside a band takes that band's colours. Illustration is optional: the language works without it, and the first band holds a slot for one once the Owner supplies artwork.
keyCharacteristics: Four flat bands, purple, sunset orange, lime and charcoal, rotating one per Section.
One theme and no theme switch; no photo; the language toggle keeps its place.
Big Shoulders Display, condensed and uppercase, sized to the band's width; Archivo for everything else.
Lists as poster billing: the category in large display type in the band's two key colours, the item in heavy uppercase Archivo in the band's ink.
One ink per band at full strength, no alpha steps; 3px ink rules and square corners.
No shadows, no blur, no gradients, no neon; an error is a dashed ink rule and its message, never a hue.

rules.name: The One Band Per Section Rule
rules.body: Every Section owns one band, and the bands rotate purple, sunset, lime, charcoal. A component never sets a palette colour; it reads the tokens of the band it sits in.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Each band has one ink at full strength: secondary, muted, hairline, control and input colours are the ink itself, and tints are transparent. On sunset any alpha step below full ink drops under 4.5:1. Three lines take another colour: the lineup's block rules are in Key; a hovered edge (`--color-hairline-hover`, `--color-input-hover`, `--color-action-hover-edge`) is the Display colour; and underlines are 3px in Key or Key Alt, on hover and while held for the language toggle, whose focus already shows the 3px ring, in Key Alt on hover and press and in Key under the current one for the Top bar's Pages, on hover and while held for the Footer's links, on hover, focus and press for band links; and linked lineup items rest on a thin underline in their row's key colour that thickens to 3px on hover, focus and press. The square between a category's items is in its row's key colour too.

rules.name: The Cream Is Large Rule
rules.body: Cream holds only 3.3:1 on sunset, so on the sunset ground it sets large type only: display, headlines, the billing keys and the Footer's title (1.375rem at 800). It also draws marks that need only 3:1: as Key Alt, underlines and the lineup's separator square, and as Display, a hovered edge. On the charcoal action fill it is the action's text, at 15:1.

rules.name: The No Error Hue Rule
rules.body: No single hue reads on all four bands, so error is the band's ink, drawn as a dashed rule with its message, never a colour alone.

rules.name: The Band-Wide Title Rule
rules.body: The Page title is sized from its container's width (24cqi, from 3.5rem to 20rem), so it runs the band's width like a poster's lettering.

rules.name: The Billing Rule
rules.body: A list is a lineup: the category in the display face at category size, above its billing, in the band's two key colours, alternating Key and Key Alt down the list; the item in heavy uppercase Archivo at billing size in the band's ink; a category's items in a row with a small square in the row's key colour between two of them; two 3px rules in Key above and below. On sunset the keys are charcoal and cream, so half the categories share the ink and stand apart by face and size.

rules.name: The Printed Flat Rule
rules.body: Nothing on About me casts or blurs; separate with a 3px ink rule or a change of band.

dos: Do give every Section one band, rotating purple, sunset, lime and charcoal, with the bar and intro on purple and the Footer on the next band in the rotation.
Do let a component read its band's tokens; never set a palette colour on a component.
Do set text in the band's one ink at full strength, and cream only at large sizes on sunset.
Do size the Page title from its container so it runs the band's width, in Big Shoulders Display, uppercase.

Do set lists as billing: the category in large display type in the band's two key colours, the item in heavy uppercase Archivo; a linked item rests on a thin underline in its category colour that thickens on hover, focus and press.
Do mark an error with a dashed 3px ink rule and its message.
Do keep the language toggle in its place and leave the theme switch out.
Do make every band work without an illustration; the slot is optional.
donts: Don't add a shadow, a blur, a gradient or neon; the bands are flat and printed.
Don't step the ink down by alpha; on sunset every step below full ink falls under 4.5:1.
Don't give error a hue; no single hue reads on all four bands.
Don't let it look like a social profile (cards, counters, feeds), a gamer or childish costume, the Portfolio recoloured, or anything corporate or cold.
Don't use Dance Gavin Dance's artwork, lettering or logo; the poster grammar is an own version.
Don't add a photo or a second theme.
Don't round a corner unless the thing is truly round.
